title: WSLUA: allow 64 bit long bitmask for ProtoField objects
description:
Mask might be specified using a (Lua) number, a string or a UInt64
object.

It is useful to handle 64 bit bitfields.

notes.body:
This MR fixes my user case: dissecting a 64 bit integer with 64 boolean fields (one for each bit)

However, my knowledge of LUA is elementary at best: I am not sure I didn't break something and I have no idea if these bitmasks were only 32 bits long in the first place for some valid reasons...

Lua uses only double internally. This means it is not able to handle 64 bit integer values by default.

I think that's the reason why a dedicated uint64 type is provided by wireshark. https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsdg_html_chunked/lua_module_Int64.html

Thanks for your reply.

I am a bit confused, though.

AFAIK:

1. This case works (a plain 64 bit field):
```
fds.test1 = ProtoField.uint64("Test_UINT64", nil, base.HEX)
tree:add(ndpi_fds.test1, tvb(offset, 8))
```
2. This case works too (a bool extracted from a 64 bit field)
```
fds.test2 = ProtoField.bool("Test_bool", nil, 64, nil, 2 ^ 4)
tree:add(ndpi_fds.test2, tvb(offset, 8))
```
3. But the same case with a bitmask longer than 32 bit doesn't work
```
fds.test2 = ProtoField.bool("Test_bool", nil, 64, nil, 2 ^ 33)   --- This is the exact case I am trying to fix
tree:add(ndpi_fds.test2, tvb(offset, 8))
```

AFAIK there are "uint64 variables" in all these cases: why is there a fundamental limitations only in 3) ?

I am probably missing something obvious here...

I can't say for sure but I think you will extend the maximum size of the bitmask to 52 or 53 bit. At this point, at the latest, the limitation that arises from the internal use of double comes into play.

If that's true: Dividing a 64 bit wide bitfield into two 32 bitfield seems to be a cleaner aproach to me than dividing it into 53 bit and 11 bit wide bitfield.

> I can't say for sure but I think you will extend the maximum size of the bitmask to 52 or 53 bit. At this point, at the latest, the limitation that arises from the internal use of double comes into play.

That is exactly the point I don't understand: 53/53 bits for the bitmask of a Bool proto field, but full 64 bits for the value of a uint64 proto field?

For my specific case I'll use two 32 bits fields anyway: the code needs to work for old Wireshark versions too.

But I am still curious if this MR is useful...

I think the difference is that lua stores any number in a double. A double looks like this:
![1280px-IEEE_754_Double_Floating_Point_Format.svg](/uploads/465e54803fe2f73a67dbdd182a425a1e/1280px-IEEE_754_Double_Floating_Point_Format.svg.png)
Sorce: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Datei:IEEE_754_Double_Floating_Point_Format.svg

So a double can use up 53 bit to store an integer number without using the exponent bits. (One of them is the sign bit) When your integer does not fit into these 53 bit the exponent comes into play and you can not save any integer number between 2^52 and 2^64. (in case of a unsigned type)

You can think of the uint64 implementation like a class which holds a C uint64 in the background and you only can access this C uint64 by the methods provided by the class. It is like a user defined type which tries to feel like a number as far as possible.

And when you define your bitmask it will be a lua number which has the limitations I just explained. I think if you really want to use 64 bit bitmasks then you must change the lua API of `ProtoField.bool()` to accet a bitmask which is given as a string or as a uint64 type. The parsing and conversion must be on the C side of the funktion.

> then you must change the lua API of `ProtoField.bool()` to accet a bitmask which is given as a string or as a uint64 type

Just out of curiosity, I might try to do that... Meanwhile, I mark this MR as draft to avoid any accidental merge

Hello, first time poster. I'm using a Lua dissector to dissect a custom protocol. All field are in 7 byte little endian number. It is decoded as uint64_le.
Bit masks used to separate out the parts. Masks with bits beyound 32 do not work. There is no error, they just show up in the tree without output bit
indicators and the values are wrong. I remembered that Lua stores everything as 'number' and it's precision is limited. The Lua API manual, to me,
implies that a mask, such as 0xffff0000000000 should be made as UInt64(0, 0xffff00). However, when I use that I get a load error that arg 5 expected a
number but got userdata. The API also says strings are OK, so I tried "0xffff0000000000" which parses with the same wrong results as no quotes, so I
tried without the 0x: "ffff0000000000": this parses with an error that the argument was a string instead of a number. I suspect this is just Lua treating
the string as a number. [[This makes me wonder what the 'string' format for masks is.]] (edited)
Is this possible? What am I doing wrong. I tried in Wireshark 3.4.0 and 4.2.2 - same results. I tried Google, looking for filed issues, even tried searching
release notes: a little tedious. (edited)
I realize I can grab different parts of the buffer as smaller values. Before moving on to that, I wanted to make sure I'm not missing something: getting
everything from the uint64 would make all the fields line up nicer in the tree.
-- Parses, but value in tree is wrong
f.cdl1_sidc = ProtoField.uint64("cdl.cdl1.sidc", "System ID Code", base.DEC, nil, 0xffff0000000000)
-- Does not parse: arg #5 expected as number, got userdata.
